content.text: I couldn't confirm this from the retrieved snippets. None of them contain the user update path, so these candidates are inferred from the standard NestJS boilerplate layout. Check the file paths and line ranges against the repository.

candidates.explanation: Most likely cause. A partial PATCH payload has no `photo`, so the merged domain entity has `photo` undefined. If `toPersistence` handles that with an unconditional `else`, or sets `photo = null` for anything falsy instead of only an explicit `null`, the save clears the photo relation. The photo should be cleared only when `photo === null` was explicitly sent. When `photo` is `undefined`, the field should be left out of the persistence entity.

`update` loads the entity, merges the partial payload over it through the mapper, and saves it. If the merge spreads `photo: undefined` or `null` from the payload over the existing photo, or rebuilds the entity from a domain object that lacks the loaded `photo` relation, the avatar is dropped on every partial update.

The service handles `photo` in the payload before calling the repository. If it normalizes a missing `photo` to `null`, or only keeps the existing one when `photo` is truthy, a name-only edit passes `photo: null` or undefined down and the avatar is removed.

fix.description: In `toPersistence`, only touch `photo` when it is explicitly provided. Set it to the mapped file when it is truthy, set it to `null` only when `photo === null`, and leave the field undefined otherwise. In `UsersRelationalRepository.update`, don't let an undefined `photo` in the payload overwrite the existing entity's photo. Also make sure `UsersService.update` doesn't default a missing `photo` to `null`.

candidates.explanation: Most likely cause. A partial PATCH payload has no `photo`, so the merged domain entity has `photo` undefined. If `toPersistence` handles that with an unconditional `else`, or sets `photo = null` for anything falsy instead of only an explicit `null`, the save clears the photo relation. The photo should be cleared only when `photo === null` was explicitly sent. When `photo` is `undefined`, the field should be left out of the persistence entity.

`update` loads the entity, merges the partial payload over it through the mapper, and saves it. If the merge spreads `photo: undefined` or `null` from the payload over the existing photo, or rebuilds the entity from a domain object that lacks the loaded `photo` relation, the avatar is dropped on every partial update.

The service handles `photo` in the payload before calling the repository. If it normalizes a missing `photo` to `null`, or only keeps the existing one when `photo` is truthy, a name-only edit passes `photo: null` or undefined down and the avatar is removed.

fix.description: In `toPersistence`, only touch `photo` when it is explicitly provided. Set it to the mapped file when it is truthy, set it to `null` only when `photo === null`, and leave the field undefined otherwise. In `UsersRelationalRepository.update`, don't let an undefined `photo` in the payload overwrite the existing entity's photo. Also make sure `UsersService.update` doesn't default a missing `photo` to `null`.
